prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, in which neutral atoms trapped at the magic wavelength enable frequency standards with fractional uncertainty near 10^-18

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single-part prize for optical lattice clocks (B057) to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. The achievement is a concrete invention, magic-wavelength trapping, with an unambiguous measured outcome: fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 with many atoms interrogated in parallel, reproduced independently in several national laboratories and compared routinely between them. It has already delivered tests of relativity and of constant variation and relativistic geodesy, and it underpins any future redefinition of the second. Katori proposed and first realised the lattice concept and Ye's group took it to record accuracy and stability, so two names carry the credit without strain. The round-1 exchange did not weaken this case. All seven B057 supporters and Eriksson, who accepts it as a good outcome, name the same pair, and the objections raised are about citation wording and timing rather than about the science. I do not treat the support count as the argument; the merits are the independent confirmation, the cleanly bounded invention and the precision it opens.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains overlap with prior recognition. The 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for controlling single quantum systems sit directly behind optical clocks, and Ye's comparisons rely on comb technology. The committee could still read the lattice clock as the best refinement of a long precision-measurement tradition rather than a new phenomenon, and the citation has to be drawn tightly enough to defend against that reading. Other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Bloom, Ludlow, Takamoto) and the ion-clock programmes are outside the credit, and I cannot verify the detailed credit split from the file. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened. Finally, B053 has a legitimate claim as a mature, widely confirmed field with a new organising principle, and its weakness is credit (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Hasan) and overlap with 2016, not worthiness.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B057 first as a discovery-plus-invention but lists the overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and Ye's partly many-body and comb-linked contribution, as the main reservation.
responses.response: I agree with your framing and take the overlap as the decisive drafting issue. I think it is answerable: the comb is a frequency-measurement tool and the 2012 prize rewards control of single trapped quantum systems, whereas magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms is a distinct idea that removes light-shift and motional errors and makes parallel interrogation possible. That is why my citation names the lattice and the magic wavelength and does not speak of optical clocks in general. On Ye, I would credit the demonstrated accuracy and stability of the lattice clock and not the broader many-body programme, which keeps the citation narrow and avoids a second achievement.

responses.point: Kroll supports B057 with two names, does not think a third name is needed, argues the redefinition of the second is a later metrological decision, and flags his stay in John Hall's laboratory for the chair to judge.
responses.response: I agree on two names and on timing. The scientific achievement is complete and independently reproduced, so the redefinition is a decision for the metrology community and not a precondition for recognition. As chair I do not consider your stay in Hall's laboratory material. Hall was honoured in 2005 for the comb, which is a different achievement, your profile records no tie to Katori or Ye, and the committee has argued openly about the 2005 overlap. I see no recusal need on B057, though I would ask you to keep the disclosure on record and I will not count it against your judgement.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B053 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp), accepts B057 as a good outcome, and says the difference is framing and weight, with the Hasan versus Mele choice and the BHZ omission as open attribution points.
responses.response: I take the new-organising-principle argument seriously, and I rank B053 as my first alternative. My difficulty is the credit. A three-name core of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp leaves out the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that the HgTe experiment tested and Hasan's three-dimensional ARPES work, and the 2016 topological-phase prize already honoured the conceptual framework. Within the three-name limit I cannot resolve that without a hard exclusion, whereas B057 has no comparable exclusion. If B057 were set aside I would support B053, but I would want the citation to be narrow, and I do not think the committee should make B053 the main configuration only because its field is larger.

responses.point: Johansson moved from circuit QED to B057 but lists the pending redefinition of the second and the credit of other groups as open points.
responses.response: Thank you for moving on the merits, and I agree that B021 is a serious later candidate given the 2025 prize and your stated recusal on it. On the redefinition, I treat it as neither a condition nor a reason to wait. The prize statutes reward the discovery and invention, which are complete, and a recognition that depended on an administrative decision would invite the wrong test. The question of other groups is real, but a fair citation that names the lattice concept and the 1e-18 demonstration can acknowledge the field's breadth in the accompanying text without adding names beyond Katori and Ye.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that a citation built on magic-wavelength lattice trapping separates the achievement sufficiently from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes.
Whether other lattice-clock contributors, such as Lemonde, Bloom, Ludlow and Takamoto, need acknowledgement beyond Katori and Ye, since I cannot verify the detailed credit split.
Whether B053 should be preferred if members weigh a new organising principle above a measurement advance, and whether its credit could be resolved within three names.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second will be read as a reason for timing, which I do not.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B057, whose field (atomic clocks) is far from my own, and I record no tie to Katori or Ye. For B054 (IceCube) I disclose only field proximity as an astroparticle physicist and a Fermi-LAT collaborator; my profile records no tie to IceCube or its credited names, and B054 is no longer my preferred configuration. As chair I considered Kroll's disclosure of a research stay in Hall's laboratory and judge recusal on B057 unnecessary.
